title: Stamp 1: Indigenismo and Mestizaje
welcome_lead: Stamp the foundational identities of Latin America.
meta_desc: A-Level Spanish adventure on indigenismo, mestizaje, and Latin American identity.

walkthroughs.body_html: From the early 20th century, intellectuals like Mariategui in Peru and the Mexican muralists Rivera, Siqueiros, Orozco championed indigenous heritage as central to national identity.
Mexican philosopher Jose Vasconcelos's La raza cosmica (1925) glorified mestizaje as Latin America's destiny. Critics later highlighted how this narrative obscured discrimination.

Many Latin American constitutions now recognise multicultural and pluri-national status. Bolivia's 2009 Constitution refounded the country as a plurinational state, recognising 36 indigenous languages.

mcqs.q: In what year was La raza cosmica published?
Does 'mestizaje' refer only to the mixing of languages?
options: Mestizaje is the name of a Mexican political party.
Mestizaje just means Spanish borrowing words from indigenous languages.
Criollo means a tourist visiting Latin America.
No - it denotes the mixing of peoples and cultures, especially European, indigenous and African heritage, central to Latin American identity.

mcqs.q: What does 'criollo' mean in the colonial and identity context?
options: Mestizaje is the name of a Mexican political party.
Criollo means a person of mixed race.
Criollo means a tourist visiting Latin America.
A person of European descent born in the Americas; 'mestizo' is the term for mixed European and indigenous heritage.

mcqs.q: Is 'indio' the preferred modern term for indigenous peoples?
options: No - 'pueblos originarios' or 'indígenas' are preferred; 'indio' is widely felt to be pejorative.
Indigenous peoples no longer exist in Latin America.
Criollo means a tourist visiting Latin America.
Indio is a neutral, standard term used in formal writing.
